description:
src/crl.rs:73 / src/ocsp.rs:79 / src/async_crl.rs:55 / src/async_ocsp.rs:58: `let mut failures: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(urls.len());` is allocated unconditionally. When the first URL succeeds (the common case for well-configured certs with one CDP), the Vec is allocated and never written to.

Cost: one allocation per check_revocation. Tiny (~24 bytes for the Vec header + a few cap-len heap bytes). At 1M revocation checks/day on a large TLS server, this is 24 MB of churn — well under noise threshold.

Mitigation: lazy allocation — only construct the Vec when we have a failure to record. This is the standard 'don't pay for the failure path on the success path' pattern.

Minor. Flagged so a future profiler-driven sweep finds it and prevents the next reviewer from re-discovering.
title: Async ocsp.rs/crl.rs: failures Vec allocated even when first URL succeeds
